industry.topic: Food services / online food delivery size
industry.fact: Redseer: India food services ~$90bn in FY26 (from $56bn in FY21), reaching ~$150bn by FY31. Online delivery's share rises from 11% (FY26) to 18% (FY31), a 20-22% CAGR.
Business Today: online food delivery 'isn't slowing down', with higher order frequency
Zomato NOV growth reached 20%+ YoY in Q1FY27 after four straight quarters of acceleration; adj EBITDA 5.6% of NOV (guidance 5-6% steady state)
Redseer (Mar-2026): QC channel for packaged F&B at ~$4bn today, rising to >$25bn GMV by 2030; packaged F&B market $100bn growing to $150bn+ by 2030

Industry estimate ~$50bn as of Apr-2026 (source unnamed); Google/Deloitte forecast $250bn by 2030. Redseer: grocery is 71% of QC GMV. UBS: discounts 19-20% recently vs 24-27% in Oct-25 to Mar-26. Blinkit, Instamart and Zepto together hold ~90% share; Flipkart Minutes, Amazon Now and BigBasket are single-digit each (Infisum)
Blinkit 2,400+ stores in 300 cities; Instamart 1,181 in 128 cities; Zepto 1,225 in 61 cities; Flipkart Minutes 1,000 MFCs in 130+ cities heading to ~1,500

Blinkit is the only major EBITDA-positive player (~Rs 3/order, Q1FY27). Instamart loses ~Rs 68/order; Zepto lost ~Rs 60/order in Q4FY26; BigBasket spent Rs 1.37 per Rs 1 of revenue in FY26; break-even needs ~1,100-1,200 orders/store/day

Confidential pre-filing with SEBI (~26-Dec-2025 / 2-Jan-2026); SEBI observations 8-May-2026; UDRHP filed 8-Jun-2026 for a Rs 8,010 cr fresh issue plus 11.35 cr-share OFS (~Rs 9,500 cr total). The UDRHP disclosed ED (FEMA) summons to the founders dated 8-Apr-2026. Raised $450m in Oct-2025 (~$7bn valuation reported). By Sep-2026 the IPO was reported on hold

Walmart's Flipkart and Amazon are expanding quick commerce aggressively and squeezing startups. Flipkart Minutes is at ~1,000 stores (750 in Mar-2026), adding ~100 a month. Amazon Now is at ~500 stores (ET via Outlook). Amazon plans to invest $48bn in India through 2030

Swiggy's foreign shareholding fell below 50% (49.76% fully diluted) in Jul-2026; it said its ownership/control status was unchanged. A shareholder vote on the IOCC cap was reported for 20-Aug-2026 (not verified from the primary source)

Budget food delivery app launched in Pune (~30-Aug-2025; meals under Rs 250, mostly Rs 100-150, no platform or packaging fee). Later expanded to Delhi NCR and 11 cities with 1m+ downloads (company release; date not verified)

Rapido's food delivery app uses a zero- or low-commission model (Inc42: flat Rs 25/order fee to restaurants vs 25-35% commissions at Zomato/Swiggy). Pilot from Aug-2025, Bengaluru citywide rollout, integrated into the main Rapido app with ~20,000 restaurants (28-Jul-2026), entered Hyderabad in Sep-2026

Management says the impact so far is limited: the same restaurants, similar or longer delivery times, and lower prices funded by lower commissions. Eternal's response is Bistro for the Rs 50-150 price point
Competitive intensity is high but more predictable. Blinkit retention: Q4 cohort retention averages 46%; NOV retention 150% at Q4 and 279% at Q12

regulation.fact: FDI policy allows foreign-owned e-commerce only in the marketplace model, not inventory. Becoming an IOCC (foreign ownership capped at 49.5%) lets Blinkit own inventory (1P). Eternal adopted the cap in Apr/May-2025 and began 1P in Q1FY26

From 22-Sep-2025, e-commerce operators are liable under section 9(5) CGST for local delivery by unregistered providers (18% GST on delivery charges collected). Legacy demands total ~Rs 447 cr (see governance)

regulation.topic: Code on Social Security - aggregator levy
regulation.fact: Codes in force from 21-Nov-2025. Aggregators contribute 1-2% of annual turnover, capped at 5% of amounts paid or payable to gig/platform workers (section 114(4)). Draft rules 30-Dec-2025 proposed eligibility of 90 days with one aggregator or 120 days across several. Social Security (Central) Rules 2026 reportedly notified 8-May-2026 (G.S.R. 344(E)), with aggregators to register workers on the portal within 45 days. The specific rate and its commencement were reportedly still not notified

Eternal helped partners unlock ~Rs 200 cr of government entitlements and is extending this to warehouse workers (target 1 lakh gig/contract workers in FY27). Active EV delivery partners rose to 100k+ by Mar-26
CCI section 26(1) investigation (initiated FY22) is ongoing
Parent's carried-forward losses are fully used in FY27, so business income at the parent becomes taxable

ownershipView.intro: Eternal has **no promoter**. Its largest holder is Info Edge (Naukri's parent, an early investor) with 12.4%; founder Deepinder Goyal owns 4.4%. Indian institutions now dominate the register: mutual funds held 31.7% at Jun-2026 and all domestic institutions 39.3%, against 29.1% for foreign investors. Two forces drove the shift: the **49.5% cap on foreign ownership** (approved by shareholders in May-2025), which keeps Eternal Indian-owned and controlled so Blinkit can own inventory; and the exit of the early foreign backers (Alipay, Antfin, Uber, SoftBank, Kuwait Investment Authority). About 4.6% sits in the employee ESOP trust.
ownershipView.source: Exchange shareholding filing for the quarter to Jun-2026 (as reproduced by Trendlyne; BSE pages blocked automated access), FY26 annual report
ownershipView.read: **Our read:** the register is now mostly long-only Indian money (index funds, flexi-cap funds, pensions), and the large foreign sellers have gone, which removes the 2023-25 supply overhang. With no promoter, there is no natural buyer of last resort, but Info Edge (12.4%) is a patient strategic holder. The 49.5% foreign cap limits how much foreign money can come back in.
